title: The Witch in Hazel
question: M's witch and her woods, ported from Messed Up Dress Up to the Livelit Playground as the Witch and Scenes slides: what do the two slides do, which layout bugs did the port turn up, what does a redraw cost, and why do the woods cost so much?

headline.what: new slides, Witch and Scenes, with 24 new controls between them; and 2 layout bugs fixed on the way
the Witch slide redrawing after one change, with the three fixes below (it was 5.0–7.5 s)
a redraw in the witch's woods, each picture new, after three fixes below: 2.6–3.5 s moving the figure, 5.2–6.4 s changing the woods. It was 10–21 s
the game drawing the same witch, or a scene
the dated update box, 2026-10-12: moving the figure in the woods redraws in a median of 1.41 s, down from 2.20 s

runtime: headless Firefox over WebDriver, a fresh profile per run, dev builds of #2635 on Matthew's laptop (the Firefox version is not stated in the report); step counts and the node harness under node

runs.Witch slide and Full Body changes: single runs, one per change ("read them as sizes rather than precise numbers"; earlier reports saw a few tenths of a second between runs of the same change)
runs.moving the figure: four changes in a series, size 100 → 90 → 100 → 90 → 100; in every series the first change after loading is the slowest
runs.update, 2026-10-12: the frame: a median over 8 changes each, with the same pictures; the points strings: measured on one build; no copy at a typed boundary: the whole redraw's median, in the same session

runs.profiles: two figure-size changes in the woods

runs.game: the median of 30 runs per setting

measures.redraw: s: a script sets a slider (input and change events) or presses a button by its label (repeated labels, such as "black", by their place in the slide), then waits until the ^picture's SVG changes, up to 60 s
measures.shapes, points: count: shapes and points in a scene's picture
measures.the worker per change: s: from request to result, split into evaluating and the gaps between slices (a slice is 5,000 trampoline steps, about 3 ms; a change was 1,292 slices)
measures.evaluation steps: count: steps of the worker's evaluation per change (610,670 in the woods, the same as the first load), and of the ^picture view's evaluation, by part of the view (the update's table)
measures.reuse checks: count: nodes from the cache (130), and failed checks by reason (no cached entry 428; a variable whose source had changed 199; a changed elaboration 18–30)
measures.bindings re-evaluated: count: top-level bindings the worker evaluates again after a figure-size change (5 after the fix)
measures.the view's own time: ms: the ^picture view's evaluation on the page (update, 2026-10-12)
measures.profile shares: share of a change: the worker about 60% evaluating and about a third encoding; the page about half evaluating the ^picture's view; profiled times run longer than real ones (two changes took 14.8 and 19.7 s profiled, against 10–15.5 s without)
measures.Game draw(): ms: draw() plus a layout read (getBBox), the median of 30 runs per setting, to the nearest millisecond
measures.memo hits: share of the view's lookups that hit (72%, the not-kept hashed memo)
measures.nodes copied: count: the picture copied whole at a typed boundary, 15,500 nodes

times: Hazel: from the slider's input and change events, or a button press, until the ^picture's SVG changes. The message timeline covered the page's posts to the eval worker and the worker's replies, with their sizes and times; the worker logged, per request, how its time went and what it reused (temporary logging). The profile: the Gecko profiler in the same headless Firefox. Step counts: under node, by kind of step and by part of the view, then timed on the page. The layout check: for every button inside a livelit, scrolled into view, its box against the livelit's box, and the element at its center. Game: draw() plus getBBox.

patches.patches/callmemo_hashed_entries.patch: the not-kept hashed memo, engine side: CallMemo keeps up to 4,096 calls per body, found by their key's hash, and counts misses only after a body's first evaluation (the patch's own comments)

provenance: No raw readings of this report survive: every number exists only as printed in the page, in its tables (tables.json) and its text (printed_in_text, above). The CPU profiles and the message timelines are not in this repository; the worker's logging and the node harness were temporary and not committed. The pictures are the slides' and the game's own SVG, rasterized, and carry no numbers.
tables_reading: In the Witch slide's table, the Game draw() cell "~1 ms, the witch with her cat and broom (3 ms on the beach)" spans five rows in the page (skin to sizes); tables.json reads cell by cell, so the four rows below it have three cells. Empty cells are empty in the page.
